newsitem.title: USA: AVIC sees $30-$40 mln revs/yr from project.
newsitem.headline: AVIC sees $30-$40 mln revs/yr from project.

text.p: AVIC Group International Inc could see revenues of $30 million to $40 million a year from its first Chinese telecommunications project starting in fiscal 1999, chairman and chief executive Joseph Wright said on Monday.
He told Reuters that revenues from the project, a cellular telephone joint venture in Hebei Province, could produce income of between $10 million and $15 million a year.

The system is scheduled to begin operating at the end of the month. AVIC holds a 31 percent stake in the joint venture made up of Hebei United Telecommunications Equipment Co and NTT International Corp, an affiliate of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.

Wright said the start of operations was important since it would mark the first time AVIC had received revenues from a Chinese project. New York-based AVIC was founded by Chinese investors to finance and develop telecommunications networks in China.
"That first dollar that comes in through the system, not the first million, I'm not just going to frame it, I'm going to blow it up," he said, tossing his head back and throwing his arms open.

Wright did not discuss expectations for the upcoming third quarter or the fiscal year. The company has generated what he called "minor revenues" from the sale of handsets and other marketing efforts, and reported a loss of $970,000, or $0.04 a share, for the second quarter ending Sept 30, 1996.

Wright, director of the federal Office of Management and Budget under former President Ronald Reagan, said he expected annual revenues of between $30 million and $40 million by roughly mid-1999 from AVIC's second project.
In that effort the company will invest $45 million to expand into and upgrade a cable television and multimedia network in Hebei, which surrounds the capital Beijing.

AVIC also has formed a joint venture with Beijing CATCH Communications Group Co to develop a nationwide paging network. Beijing CATCH has an option to acquire 45 percent of AVIC and is a subsidiary of Hainan Minyuan Modern Agricultural Development Co.
The company plans to expand into the Beijing paging market by the end of the year and sees "fairly steady" cash flow of $4 million to $6 million annually from the service, Wright said.
AVIC also has signed a memorandum of understanding with the government of Sichuan Province for a cellular telephone service.

AVIC's shares have fallen from a brief high of 15 in March 1996, when AVIC traded among bulletin board stocks, to 1-1/2 in October. The shares began trading on the American Stock Exchange in November and closed on Monday at 2-3/4, up 1/8.
Wright called bulletin baord trade "a swamp" and attributed the decline to short selling and a tailing off of initially strong buying by Chinese investors.
"When it first came out, there was a great anticipation that their baby was coming to market," he said.
